title: [BugFix][Worker] Preserve graph eligibility on P/D decode nodes
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Apply the existing prompt-tail batch reclassification to pure P/D decode nodes (`kv_consumer` without `kv_producer`), independently of whether the recompute scheduler is enabled.

After KV transfer, a newly admitted decode request can still be marked as prefilling on its first verification step. When that step finishes the prompt tail and schedules exactly `decode_query_len` tokens, the batch can have a uniform decode shape, but `has_prefill` prevents uniform-token classification and graph replay. With data parallelism, one rank falling back to eager can force the other ranks to do the same.

This change only replaces the role gate of the existing reclassification block. The per-request eligibility checks and scheduling behavior are unchanged. Regression tests cover KV roles, single-token and speculative decode, incomplete prompt tails, remaining prefill requests, and dummy batches.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible decode-shaped prompt-tail batches on pure P/D decode nodes can use captured graphs even when the recompute scheduler is disabled. No API, CLI, or configuration changes are introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

- Updated `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2.py` with regression coverage for consumer-only, producer-only, dual-role, and non-P/D configurations; query lengths 1, 2, and 4; unfinished prefill; and dummy batches. The existing prompt-tail input preparation regression now uses a consumer configuration.
- Local isolated execution of the production `gather_batch_req_state` method against the repository regression tests: 10 cases passed. The upstream batch-state method and uniform-token helper were mocked; this validates the local reclassification logic only.
- Ruff lint, Ruff format checks, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Standard pytest collection was blocked because the local Windows environment does not have `vllm` installed. The full `format.sh ci` check was blocked by missing `pre-commit`. Full UT and NPU integration validation remain for CI; no new hardware benchmark was run for these commits.

Previously reported hardware measurements for the same role-gate change used MiniMax-M3 W8A8, Mooncake P/D transfer, a DP4 x TP4 decode node, the v2 runner with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, and EAGLE3 with three speculative tokens. The workload used streaming arrivals with 2048-token GSM8K inputs. These are historical measurements from the original experiment, not a benchmark of this commit; the tested variant also included eager-fallback diagnostic logging.

| Metric | Baseline (120 samples) | Role-gate change (40 samples) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Median TPOT | 44.5 ms | 20.7 ms |
| Median ITL | 80.1 ms | 67.2 ms |
| P90 ITL | 633.1 ms | 72.8 ms |
| Mean ITL | 157.2 ms | 68.1 ms |

The original experiment also reported three passing deterministic correctness spot checks, no eager-fallback warnings, and no runtime graph captures. The unequal sample counts and small correctness sample limit the conclusions.
